paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, comparing the accuracy of various methods as the co-occurrence number increases. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number", is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to 3000, with tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is on a linear scale, ranging from 40 to 65, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The plot includes six lines representing different editing methods: Base (black, circle marker, solid line), FT (blue, triangle marker, solid line), IKE (red, triangle marker, solid line), MEND (brown, diamond marker, solid line), MEMIT (purple, triangle marker, solid line), and ROME (green, square marker, solid line). The Base model starts at around 39% and increases to approximately 44% as the co-occurrence number rises. The FT line begins at around 40% and rises to about 48%. The IKE line starts at roughly 44% and reaches approximately 50%. The MEND line begins at around 46% and increases to about 57%. The MEMIT line starts at approximately 44% and rises to around 55%. The ROME line begins at roughly 51% and reaches approximately 66%. All lines exhibit an overall upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases.
